basis: Alice holds the curtain anchor and dries her eyes; at t=1.5 her look goes screen-left up the hall, her first outward look in four shots. The White Rabbit runs his ne_entrance -> lamp_row_mid -> glass_table -> curtain line: he comes out of the dark corner entrance on four legs with the gloves and fan in his mouth, is level with the middle of the hall at t=2.0, passes the glass table at t=4.6 and pulls up on his haunches at (7.60, -1.80) at t=5.4 - 1.59 m short of the giant girl, 'a few feet short' as the map says. He is staged as kind=creature throughout, per the H3S ruling: four legs, things carried in the mouth, never upright and never given hands, and his gaze never goes to Alice or to the lens.
warnings: sh072 reproduces the sh069 set-up exactly (same position, target, lens) - camera.json calls it 'back to the sh068 close across the hall', but sh068 is a 28 mm and sh072 a 50 mm, so the 50 mm frame is the one that matches.

sh073: the Rabbit reads about 0.04 of frame height at the top of the shot instead of composition's 0.14, because he is 11.6 m up the hall at that instant and a 40 mm cannot make him larger from there. He grows to about 0.20 as he comes on.
He covers the 17 m from the corner entrance in 5.4 s (peak 3.3 m/s) to hit the written beats - fast for a rabbit wading four inches of water, but the beats are frozen.
Closest approach Alice/Rabbit is 1.59 m at t=5.4 (her 0.38 m seated half-depth against his 0.18 m), well clear of the 0.20 m reference separation.
